question: What makes it possible for a robot to build?

answer.answer:
**Summary**

Building work gets done by a machine when six things line up: an arm to do the work (RE2), a planned path for it to follow (PR12), components standardised enough that the same motion works every time (AT7), a mobile factory around the work (CO12), prefabrication upstream (PR2), and a delivery model and work culture that will carry it (RI12). Only one of those six is a machine; the other five are process, standardisation, environment and organisation, so the hard part of making a robot build is rarely the robot. Two of the six are asserted in the literature and almost unexhibited: the mobile factory precondition is carried by none of the 50 coded cases and the path-planning link by 2, while the arm is carried by 12 and standardisation by 10. Note that the record codes this activity as robotic assembly rather than as robots as such, so everything below is about the assembly process.

**The detailed answer**

**The anchor.** PR4 "Robotic assembly" (Process) carries 4 inbound and 6 outbound dependency edges, all of them listed in the context, and 13 of the 50 coded cases draw on it. [1] Its requirement side is complete, so the six below can be quoted as the full cited set of what has to be in place.

**What has to be in place, with how much of the record carries each:**

- RE2 "Robotic arm" enablesCapability PR4 (DEP11), backed by peer-reviewed evidence and carried by 12 of the 50 coded cases [1], reciprocated by DEP24, PR4 dependsOn RE2, also carried by 12: robotic assembly requires a robot arm [1]. 22 of the 50 cases draw on RE2 in its own right. [1] This is the only Resource among PR4's requirements.
- AT7 "Highly standardised" (Attribute) enablesCapability PR4 (DEP88), carried by 10 of the 50, on the finding that Japanese automated erection systems rely on standardised prefabricated components. [1] 25 of the 50 cases draw on AT7. [1]
- PR12 "Path-planning" (Process) enablesCapability PR4 (DEP23), carried by 2 of the 50, on the claim that path planning is a precondition for robotic assembly. [1] 26 of the 50 cases draw on PR12. [1] The gap between 26 and 2 is the sharp point here: path-planning is common in the record, but the coded cases rarely carry it together with robotic assembly.
- CO12 "Mobile factory" (Condition) enablesCapability PR4 (DEP42), peer-reviewed, carried by 0 of the 50 coded cases. [1] Only 1 of the 50 cases draws on CO12 at all. [1] This is a direct cited precondition of robotic assembly that no case in the record exhibits alongside it.
- PR4 hasPrecondition PR2 "Prefabrication/off-site" (DEP55), carried by 4 of the 50, on the basis that automated overhead delivery and assembly requires extensive prefabrication and unification of materials. [1] 20 of the 50 cases draw on PR2. [1]
- PR4 dependsOn RI12 "Delivery/business model/work culture" (DEP61), carried by 2 of the 50: robotics adoption in precast production rests on the environmental and organisational context. [1] 16 of the 50 cases draw on RI12. [1]

**One step further up, on the path-planning branch.** PR12 hasPrecondition RE4 "3D scanner/sensor/camera/ICT" (DEP39), carried by 22 of the 50, since localisation via onboard sensors is a fundamental prerequisite for autonomous operation [1], and PR12 dependsOn CO16 "3D point-cloud" (DEP30), carried by 9 [1]. RE1 "Parametric/computational/data-driven algorithm/machine code" enables PR12 (DEP7, carried by 7) [1] and RE8 "Machine Learning/AI algorithm" enables PR12 (DEP3, carried by 5) [1], while RI5 "Location dependent/site constraint" constrains PR12 (DEP44, carried by 15), because reliable GNSS signals are typically unavailable indoors [1].

**What it yields.** PR4 amplifies VA2 "Reduce time/improve productivity/efficiency" (DEP95, carried by 13) [1], amplifies VA6 "Reduce cost" (DEP54, carried by 7) [1] and enablesCapability VA10 "Reduce errors/constraints" (DEP21, carried by only 1) [1]. 49 of the 50 coded cases draw on VA2 [1], so the productivity motive is near-universal even where the assembly edge itself is thin.

**People are not removed.** RE6 "Significant human involvement" is drawn on by 50 of the 50 coded cases and carries no dependency edge at all [1], and 44 of the 50 draw on RI6 "Require workforce training" [1]. CO6 "Human-robot interaction" dependsOn RI6 (DEP34, carried by 27), because the success of human-robot collaboration is contingent on a skilled workforce [1], and CO6 mitigates RI20 "Work safety concern" (DEP57, standards evidence, carried by 4) through power-and-force-limiting collaborative operation [1]. RI20 carries 3 cited edges in total, of which only CO6's appears here [1], so I cannot say how many paths reach it.

**Deployed record.** The context carries several census processes that actually perform assembly. census_RXH1-1 was adopted to address integration and performs assembly, steelwork and welding on the structural core and the building envelope, facade or curtain wall, at technology readiness level 9 [2]; its manufacturer is Firm_013. census_RXH7-2 was adopted to address quality, safety, labor and market, and performs assembly and tiling on the building envelope, facade or curtain wall, at technology readiness level 9 [3], with Firm_125 as manufacturer and a link to process RP29. census_RXH4-1 addresses cost and labor and performs assembly and concrete work on the structural core and envelope, at technology readiness level 9 [4] (Firm_166), census_RXH3-2 addresses digital and cost concerns and performs assembly, steelwork and welding, at technology readiness level 9 [5] (developed by Firm_143), and census_RXM11-6 addresses cost and integration, performing 3d printing, concrete work, shotcrete and surface treatment, at technology readiness level 7 [6] (Firm_020 and Firm_151). The context does not link any of these records to individual enablers, so I cannot say which of RE2, AT7, PR12, CO12, PR2 or RI12 each one exhibits.

**A caution on reading.** The cited dependency layer is sparse and uneven, with 100 edges touching 68 of the 140 enablers, so 72 carry no cited edge at all, which is a property of the literature rather than of the record. [1] The requirement list above is complete for PR4, but the absence of an edge elsewhere does not mean an enabler is absent or unimportant.
